newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down on campaign uneasiness.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down on campaign uneasiness.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended sharply down on Thursday due to worries about rising political tensions and a spill-over from steep falls in the Thai market, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index closed 13.30 points, or 1.98 percent, down at 656.99 points after touching a day-low of 655.01 points. Decliners led advancers by 94 to 20 with 67 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 474 billion rupiah against 473 billion rupiah on Wednesday.
"Some party supporters are getting too excited about the election campaign. This has led to some clashes yesterday and this afternoon," one analyst with a foreign brokerage firm said.
The analyst said he expected sentiment to remain cautious on Friday due to the campaign for May 29 general elections, while profit-taking was likely to continue particularly on big-caps.

On Wednesday, clashes between supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and security forces marred campaigning in Central Java province and the capital Jakarta, police said on Thursday.
Several people were hurt in a clash in Jakarta on Thursday between supporters of the ruling Golkar party and construction site workers, witnesses said.

One sales manager with a large brokerage firm said Indonesia's economic fundamentals remained firm and should remain so the rest of the year and that the falls should provided opportunities for bargain hunting.
Analysts said the correction had earlier been expected following recent rises in index-linked stocks, but the falls were much higher than expected.
Big-caps Gudang Garam, Sampoerna, Telkom and Indosat were among the losers following the sell-off, brokers said.
Tyre-cord manufacturer Branta Mulia rose 200 rupiah to close at 3,125 rupiah amid reports that U.S.-based Du Pont planned to buy a 19.91 percent stake in the firm, brokers said.

The most actively traded small tourism services firm Bayu Buana was unchanged at 1,500 rupiah, with some 36 million shares traded on market talk of a possible take-over, brokers said. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
